doc.title: Joe Williams interviewed by Leslie Gourse, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996

title: Not sticking his neck out: Basie discouraging new arrangements
summary: Williams says he just sings what he feels like; Basie would discourage him from asking for new arrangements, then nod when the audience approved.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: And I wanted to ask you, Joe, you know you’ve had such a wonderful, successful career. And I once did ask you, how did you know to make the right decisions for yourself? What guided you? And you answered me, you said, “Oh, every day, every day.” Now I really don’t know if you meant the song gave you such a wonderful boost, I mean the great hit that you had with Basie, or did you just mean that you learned every day as you went along to take risks and to stick your neck out, and to enjoy the fruits of your successes.
I never have thought I was sticking my neck out.

No, no. You do what you do. I sing. And if I feel like I want to sing something I do it. I used to have some problems with Mr. Basie sometimes. I would ask, I’d say, “Hey, Bas’, I’d like to get an arrangement on” such and such a song. And he’d say, “Oh, you don’t need that thing. Sing the things you’ve been singing.” You know. If you let people, even those closest to you — and he was very close to me — if you let them discourage you from doing what you feel you want to do, in many instances it’ll leave you one dimensional as opposed to being a person of some variety. So consequently you have to fight even those that you love and those that are closest to you. Because I remember after bugging him for a long time to do something, when we finally did it, and the audience approval was so enthusiastic, he would look at me and he would nod his head.
